title: Termwise coproducts in a Grothendieck derived category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be the localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every set $I$ in the chosen indexing universe and family of unbounded cochain complexes $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$, the termwise coproduct complex $(\bigoplus_iK_i)^r=\bigoplus_i K_i^r$, with differential induced by the $d_i^r$, exists. Its image $Q(\bigoplus_iK_i^\bullet)$, with the images of the termwise coprojections, is a coproduct of the $Q(K_i^\bullet)$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. The assertion includes the empty set.

proof.text: The Grothendieck hypothesis gives coproducts in the indexing universe and K-injective resolutions, by the source-library instance Abelian.hasKInjectiveResolutions_of_isGrothendieckAbelian. The resolution uses exactly the functorial K-injective construction already recorded by lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence.

Reuse the already-proved generic cofan construction CategoryTheory.derivedCoproductCofan in Sheaf.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckDerivedCoproducts (the construction proving lem-grothendieck-derived-has-coproducts). Take E_i = Q(K_i) and the representative isomorphisms to be identities. This gives the colimit cofan with vertex Q(coproduct K) and legs Q(Sigma.ι K i). The construction already assembles chain maps and homotopies and compares them with derived maps into K-injective resolutions; it includes the empty family. Apply isColimitMapCoconeCofanMkEquiv to regard this as the mapped coproduct cocone. Then preservesColimit_of_preserves_colimit_cocone shows that Q preserves the colimit of Discrete.functor K.

Mathlib HomologicalComplex.isColimitCoconeOfHasColimitEval proves that the specified termwise cocone is a colimit in the category of complexes. Apply isColimitOfPreserves for Q to this cocone, using the preservation instance just obtained, and wrap the resulting IsColimit in Nonempty. Preservation applies to this exact cocone, so the images of its specified coprojections are retained. No boundedness or nonemptiness assumption is introduced.
